clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old man developed progressive ascending symmetrical muscle weakness and distal paraesthesia approximately two weeks after COVID-19 ChAdOx1 vaccination. On admission, cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated protein (1.77 g/L) with normal glucose and white cell count, consistent with albuminocytologic dissociation. Nerve conduction studies showed patchy attenuation of upper limb motor responses without definitive demyelination, likely due to early disease stage. MRI of the whole spine revealed globally thickened cauda equina nerve rootlets with prominent ventral nerve root and conus medullaris pial enhancement, supporting an inflammatory autoimmune neuropathy. MRI of the brain was normal, excluding central nervous system pathology. This integrated clinical presentation, CSF findings, electrophysiological study, and imaging are diagnostic and supportive of GBS.
